title: University of Aden appointed academics’ strike (reported onset disputed)
location: University of Aden colleges in southern governorates; exact workplace and any public gathering are not reported. S038 names Aden, Lahj, Abyan, al-Dhale and Shabwa; S044 names Aden, Lahj, al-Dhale and Shabwa.
scope: Reported multi-governorate university teaching stoppage; geographic accounts differ.
organizer: Appointed University of Aden academics; S038 quotes coordinator Fahmi al-Haboub, while S044 cites committee head Ali al-Qahtani. Their relationship is unresolved.
participants_original: S044 reports 927 of 1,300 appointed academics began a strike. This is an employee/striker figure, not a count of people gathered. S038 gives no participant count.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Neither report describes a public gathering or simultaneous attendance; the 927 figure counts employees reported on strike, not a crowd.

title.summary: Both articles report a University of Aden appointed-academics teaching strike; whether they describe the same start or separate stages remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: S044 dates the reported start to Wednesday 20 January; S038 says the strike began “today” on Saturday 23 January. Preserve the conflict and leave physical onset unknown.

end_date.summary: Neither article establishes a physical end or resumption.

location.summary: S038 lists five governorates; S044 lists four. Neither identifies a gathered crowd or local turnout.

scope.summary: Both describe a University-wide teaching stoppage across colleges; geographic coverage differs.

organizer.summary: S038 quotes coordinator Fahmi al-Haboub; S044 attributes its account to Ali al-Qahtani. Coordination between them is not established.

demands.summary: Reports cite financial adjustment, salaries/incentives and appointment/posting procedures. The wage-related demand supports the broad labor_wage_dispute category.

participants_original.summary: The article reports 927 of 1,300 appointed academics on strike; that denominator/count describes employees, not gathered participants.

participants_min.summary: Neither gives a numeric count of people assembled; no attendance bound is assigned.

participants_max.summary: Neither gives a numeric count of people assembled; no attendance bound is assigned.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A reported employee strike does not establish a public meeting of at least 50.

state_target.summary: S038 quotes an appeal to Prime Minister Maeen Abdulmalik; S044 describes alleged University/government delay and appointment/wage demands. The University is also an employer/decision-maker.

protester_violence.summary: Neither report describes violence by participants; silence remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No response to the reported strike is described.

state_response.ignore.summary: Alleged prior delay is part of the grievance; no event-specific avoidance/refusal is established.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-related state killing is reported.

start_precision.summary: Unknown because the reported start dates conflict (20 and 23 January).

end_precision.summary: Unknown; neither source establishes a physical end.

eligibility.summary: Pending threshold because no public gathering or simultaneous attendee count is documented; the 927 figure is employees on strike.

notes: Two opened reports conflict on the strike date (20 versus 23 January), spokesperson, and governorate list. S044 says “agencies” without identifying one; S038 is a local bylined report. They are not treated as independent corroboration. No public assembly or turnout is established. The strike is a lead for review, not an approved MM event.
open_questions: Was this one stoppage or more than one stage/action?
What was the physical first day and did teaching resume?
Did any workers assemble publicly, and was a simultaneous count of at least 50 reported?
Did the Yemen government or University respond to this specific strike?

title: Aden Refinery workers’ allowance strike (onset and public gathering unverified)
location: Aden Refinery and fuel distribution in Aden. No off-site gathering location is documented.
scope: Local workplace labor action with reported city-wide fuel-supply effects.
organizer: Aden Refinery workers and worker committee; relation to other Aden oil-company union groups is unverified.
participants_original: No strike or gathering count is reported. S004 says annual allowances were owed to more than 3,500 employees; that is a payroll figure, not strikers or gathered participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The sources report a workplace strike and its fuel effects but give no number of workers assembled or evidence of a public gathering.

title.summary: S004 reports an ongoing Aden refinery workers’ strike; S047 reports a one-week suspension and committee meeting.

start_date.summary: S004 says fuel stations had been closed since the previous Friday relative to its 19 January publication (15 January), but does not explicitly date the strike’s physical start. S047 gives no onset. Leave onset unknown and unit ownership open.

end_date.summary: S047 reports a one-week suspension beginning 21 January, not a verified physical end or permanent return to work.

location.summary: The employer and fuel disruption are in Aden; no public meeting location is given.

scope.summary: S004 attributes city fuel disruption to the refinery workers’ strike; this does not describe a mass public gathering.

organizer.summary: S047 identifies worker-committee representatives in the meeting; no complete organization membership or relation to other unions is established.

demands.summary: S004 reports unpaid annual allowances and requests to government; S047 says officials and committee would address worker demands.

participants_original.summary: No participant count. The 3,500-plus employee reference in S004 concerns owed allowances.

participants_min.summary: No gathered-participant count or numeric bound.

participants_max.summary: No gathered-participant count or numeric bound.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Work stoppage and city fuel impact do not establish a public gathering of 50.

state_target.summary: S004 describes repeated requests to the Yemen government to address arrears. S047 names the Deputy Minister of Oil and Aden deputy governor among officials meeting worker representatives.

protester_violence.summary: Neither source reports violence by strikers; silence remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Officials met worker representatives and formed a joint committee to address demands. This is an accommodation/hearing, not proof that demands were met.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No gathering or dispersal is reported.

state_response.ignore.summary: Earlier unresolved requests are grievance context; sources do not establish event-specific refusal/avoidance.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-related state killing is reported.

start_precision.summary: Unknown because the 15 January fuel-station closure date is not explicitly the strike onset.

end_precision.summary: Unknown because a one-week suspension is not a verified physical end.

eligibility.summary: Pending unit ownership because the physical strike onset is not dated and may precede January; public assembly size is also unreported.

notes: S004 dates fuel-station closures to the prior Friday, 15 January, but its wording does not make that the confirmed strike onset. S047 reports a one-week suspension from 21 January. Its earlier saved summary dates the meeting to 20 January, while the retained read_scope labels the substantive paragraphs as concerning the “21 January meeting”; the retained record cannot resolve the meeting day. The suspension is not an established physical end. S045 returned HTTP 200 but the article title/body were not exposed; S006 remains search-only because a previous Al-Araby publisher request returned 403. No gathering threshold is shown, and onset could place ownership outside January.
open_questions: When did refinery workers physically stop work?
Did the stoppage begin in January or before it?
Did at least 50 workers assemble publicly, or was this only a workplace stoppage?
Did operations resume after the one-week suspension?
Were arrears resolved or did action recur in February?
Are other media reports independent or based on the same committee statement?

title: Southern Teachers Syndicate announced work stoppage (execution unverified)
location: Aden and/or southern Yemen schools; the full geographic coverage is not established.
scope: Announcement of recurring Sunday/Monday school stoppages through mid-February; execution and episode form are unknown.
organizer: General Syndicate of Southern Teachers in Aden / Southern Teachers Syndicate; exact organization naming and branch relationship need review.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. No body confirms execution, a public gathering, or the number of teachers who stopped work or assembled.

title.summary: The articles describe a planned southern teachers’ strike; neither confirms it occurred.

start_date.summary: S012 published 21 January and says strikes would start the following week; S029’s 24 January, 9:11 p.m. page says a Sunday start is upcoming. The intended day is ambiguous; no physical onset is established.

end_date.summary: The announced program through mid-February is not a verified physical end.

location.summary: S012 refers to Aden; broader southern school coverage is not specified consistently.

scope.summary: Both report planned repeated stoppages, but occurrence and episode boundaries are unverified.

organizer.summary: Both name the Southern Teachers Syndicate/union; exact relationship between named bodies is not independently established.

demands.summary: The article lists unpaid statutory/work-nature allowances and contractor entitlements; S012 says the government was asked to respond but supplies no detail.

participants_original.summary: Neither gives a number of strikers or gathered participants.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Announcement of a work stoppage does not establish execution, a public meeting, or 50 attendees.

state_target.summary: S012 conditions escalation on the Yemen government response. S029 addresses responsible authorities and separately mentions coalition leadership/UN messages; the exact responsible domestic authority is not fully resolved.

protester_violence.summary: No action-body evidence about participant violence; unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No response to an executed January action is established.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No executed gathering or dispersal is reported.

state_response.ignore.summary: A threatened escalation if government does not respond is not proof of an event-specific refusal.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-related state killing is reported.

start_precision.summary: Unknown because the intended Sunday is ambiguous and execution is unverified.

end_precision.summary: Unknown; announced duration/program through mid-February is not a physical end.

eligibility.summary: Pending evidence because these are strike announcements without verified execution, public assembly or turnout.

notes: Preserve as an announcement lead only. S012 reports Sunday/Monday stoppages from the following week, through mid-February, and a threatened wider strike if government did not respond. S029 is dated Sunday 24 January at 9:11 p.m. but uses forward-looking Sunday wording; the intended first date is unclear. No executed strike, public assembly, participant count or event-specific state response is established. February S014 describes a later renewed escalation after a 10 February meeting; it does not prove January execution or physical continuity.
open_questions: What was its actual start date and did the date refer to 24 or 31 January?
How many teachers stopped work, and did any group assemble publicly?
What locations and school groups participated?
Was the February announcement a continuation, new escalation or distinct action?
Which domestic authority was responsible for each allowance demand?
